AGENDA
  CITY COUNCIL MEETING
  DECEMBER 15, 2020
UNTIL FURTHER NOTICE, MEETINGS WILL BE CONDUCTED PURSUANT TO THE PROVISIONS OF THE
GOVERNOR'S EXECUTIVE ORDERS N-25-20, N-29-20, AND N-35-20, WHICH ALLOWS MEETINGS TO BE
VIDEOCONFERENCED WITHOUT PROVIDING A PHYSICAL LOCATION. TO PROVIDE COMMENTS
DURING A MEETING, EITHER SEND AN EMAIL TO: publiccomments@norwalkca.gov OR CALL (669) 900-
6833; MEETING ID: 709 573 2685; PASSCODE: 784059 DURING THE MEETING TO SPEAK ON AN ITEM
OR UNDER ORAL COMMUNICATIONS. THE MEETING MAY BE VIEWED ON FIOS CHANNEL 32 OR
CHARTER CHANNEL 3 OR ON THE CITY'S WEBPAGE AT: https://www.norwalk.org/city-hall/meeting-
agendas-393.
  6:15 PM
  VIDEOCONFERENCE
  AND VIA VIDEOCONFERENCE

  Jennifer Perez, Mayor
  Tony Ayala, Vice Mayor
  Rick Ramirez, Councilmember
  Margarita L. Rios, Councilmember
  Ana Valencia, Councilmember
  Public Comment: Comments may be made in person, submitted via email at: publiccomments@norwalkca.gov, or through
  the video conference during the designated time on any item on the agenda or on any other matter within the jurisdiction
  subject to the rules of decorum described in Norwalk Municipal Code §2.08.020. The maximum time allowed is three
  minutes.

  Pursuant to provisions of the Brown Act, no action may be taken on a matter unless it is listed on the agenda, or unless
  certain emergency or special circumstances exist. The City Council may direct staff to investigate and/or schedule certain
  matters for consideration at a future City Council meeting.

  Please adhere to the following procedures when addressing the Council:

  • Comments should be limited to 3 minutes or less.
  • Comments should be directed to the City Council as a whole and not directed to individual Councilmembers.

  Americans with Disabilities Act: In compliance with the ADA, if you need special assistance to participate in a City
  meeting or other services offered by this City, please contact the City Clerk's Department, (562) 929-5720. Assisted listening
  devices are available at this meeting. Ask the City Clerk if you desire to use this device. Upon request, the agenda and
  documents in the agenda packet can be made available in appropriate alternative formats to persons with a disability.
  Notification of at least 48 hours prior to the meeting or time when services are needed will assist the City staff in assuring
  that reasonable arrangements can be made to provide accessibility to the meeting or service.

  Note: Any writings and/or documents provided to a majority of the City Council regarding any item on this agenda after it
  has been posted will also be made available for public inspection.

  Writings and/or documents are available for inspection in the City Clerk's Department, City Hall, 12700 Norwalk Boulevard
  during regular business hours, 8:00 a.m. to 6:00 p.m., Monday - Thursday and 8:00 a.m. to 5:00 p.m., every other Friday;
  telephone (562) 929-5720. You may also contact the City Clerk via e mail at recordsrequests@norwalkca.gov.

  STUDY SESSION MEETING – 5:00 p.m.
 CALL TO ORDER
  Mayor Perez

ROLL CALL
  Theresa Devoy, CMC
  City Clerk

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS FOR CLOSED SESSION MATTERS

CLOSED SESSION

  I.  CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE §54957(a):
  THREAT TO PUBLIC SERVICES OR FACILITIES – Consultation with the City Manager, Los Angeles
  County Sheriff representative, and other related City officials.

  II.  CONFERENCE WITH REAL PROPERTY NEGOTIATOR PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT CODE
  §54956.8: APN 8056-017-901; Negotiating Parties: Jesus M. Gomez, City Manager, on behalf of the
  City and Penny Reeves, Aquirecorp (Norwalk Auto Auction); Under Negotiation: Price and Terms of
  Payment.

  III.  CONFERENCE WITH LEGAL COUNSEL – EXISTING LITIGATION PURSUANT TO GOVERNMENT
  CODE §54956.9(d)(1): County of Los Angeles vs. City of Norwalk, LASC Case No. 20STCP01480.

RECESS

  REGULAR MEETING – 6:00 p.m.

CALL TO ORDER
  Mayor Perez

INVOCATION
  Jim Parker
  Executive Director of Regional Transportation

FLAG SALUTE
  Jesenia Sanchez
  Principal Human Resources Analyst

ROLL CALL
  Theresa Devoy, CMC
  City Clerk

CITY COUNCIL COMMENTS

  a.  Report of City Council Travel

SPECIAL PRESENTATIONS
  City Council to recognize Carolina Velasquez and Saeed Amirazizi on their retirements from the City.

CITY MANAGER COMMENTS

  1.  COVID-19 Update.

  2.  Virtual Tree Lighting Ceremony and Angel Tree Project recap.

CLOSED SESSION REPORT

CONSENT CALENDAR

Consent calendar items are considered routine matters which may be enacted by one motion and roll call vote.
Any item may be removed from the consent calendar and considered separately by City Council.
   1.  MEETING MINUTES – Staff recommends City Council approve the minutes of the meeting of
  December 1, 2020. 825-04

  Minutes

  2.  PAYROLL – Staff recommends City Council approve the payroll for the period November 1, 2020 –
  November 14, 2020, in the total amount of $884,216.62. 630

  Report

  3.  COMMERCIAL DEMANDS – Staff recommends City Council approve the warrant register period
  November 25, 2020 - December 8, 2020, in the total amount of $1,004,459.22. 640

  Report

  4.  CLAIMS AGAINST THE CITY – Staff recommends City Council deny the claims filed by Billie Mealy
  and Julia Carlos Orozco. 830-13/15

  Report

  5.  CONFIRM EMERGENCY WORK AT 11203 LAKELAND ROAD – STEPHEN DORECK EQUIPMENT
  RENTALS, INC. - Staff recommends City Council confirm the emergency service line repair work at
  11203 Lakeland Road, completed by Stephen Doreck Equipment Rentals, Inc., in the amount of
  $5,890.53. 955

  Report

  6.  ORDINANCE NO. 20-1720 – AMENDING TITLE NUMBERS 5 AND 17 OF THE NORWALK
  MUNICIPAL CODE - Staff recommends City Council accept for second reading and adopt Ordinance
  No. 20-1720, AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY OF NORWALK AMENDING TITLE 5 OF THE
  NORWALK MUNICIPAL CODE AS IT RELATES TO SPECIAL EVENTS AND PAWNBROKERS AND
  TITLE 17 OF THE NORWALK MUNICIPAL CODE AS IT RELATES TO DEFINITIONS, APPROVAL
  PROCEDURES, SPECIFIC USE REQUIREMENTS, OFF-STREET PARKING AND LOADING
  REQUIREMENTS, SIGN STANDARDS, AND PERMITTED LAND USES AND FINDING THE
  ORDINANCE EXEMPT FROM THE CALIFORNIA ENVIRONMENTAL QUALITY ACT. 320-05-320

  Report

  7.  AGREEMENT AMENDMENT NO. 8 AND TERM EXTENSION – ADVANCED RESERVATION DIAL-A-
  RIDE / SUBSCRIPTION SERVICE – Staff recommends City Council approve Amendment No. 8 and
  Term extension with MV Transportation, Inc. to provide Advanced Reservation Dial-A-Ride/Subscription
  Services through March 31, 2021 in the amount of $85,696; and authorize the City Manager to execute
  the amendment, on behalf of the City, in a form approved by the City Attorney. 1120-07

  Report

  8.  AGREEMENT AMENDMENT NO. 4 AND TERM EXTENSION – PARATRANSIT USER SIDE SUBSIDY
  TRANSPORTATION PROGRAM – Staff recommends City Council approve Amendment No. 4 and
  Term extension with Fiesta Taxi Cooperative, Inc. to provide Paratransit User Side Subsidy
  Transportation Program through February 28, 2021 in the amount of $10,834; and authorize the City
  Manager to execute the amendment, on behalf of the City, in a form approved by the City Attorney.
  1120-07

  Report

APPOINTMENTS

  9.  ADVISORY BODIES – Staff recommends City Council make appointments to fill the vacancies on the
  various City advisory bodies. 200

  Report

10. ORDINANCE NO. 20-1721 – ELECTRONIC CAMPAIGN DISCLOSURE DOCUMENTS AND STATEMENT
   OF ECONOMIC INTERESTS FILING – AGREEMENT TO PROVIDE ELECTRONIC FILING SYSTEM –
  Staff recommends City Council:

  a.  introduce for first reading by title only Ordinance No. 20-1721, AN ORDINANCE OF THE CITY OF
  NORWALK ADDING CHAPTER 2.09 TO THE NORWALK MUNICIPAL CODE REGARDING
  CAMPAIGN DISCLOSURE DOCUMENTS AND STATEMENTS OF ECONOMIC INTERESTS, and
  waive further reading; and

  b.  approve an agreement with NetFile to implement an electronic filing system for campaign disclosure
  documents and Statements of Economic Interests in the amount of $6,900 annually for five years; and
  authorize the City Manager to execute the agreement and any amendments provided there is funding
  in budget, on behalf of the City, in a form approved by the City Attorney. 865-04/05

  Report

REPORTS

  11. CALIFORNIA POLYTECHNIC STATE UNIVERSITY, SAN LUIS OBISPO – STUDIO PROJECT –
  NORWALK STRATEGIC PLAN - Staff recommends City Council receive and file this report. 152

  Report

  12. AMENDMENT NO. 2 TO THE GROUND LEASE AGREEMENT FOR THE PROPERTY AT 12405
  ROSECRANS AVENUE – Staff recommends City Council approve Amendment No. 2 with Aquirecorp
  for a term of two years including an option to extend for one two-year period; and authorize the City
  Manager to execute Amendment No. 2 on behalf of the City, in a form approved by the City Attorney.
  925-02

  Report

  13. FIRESTONE BOULEVARD/SAN ANTONIO DRIVE CORRIDOR STUDY – Staff recommends City
  Council receive and file this report.

  Report

  14. LOS ANGELES METRO’S FARELESS SYSTEM INITIATIVE UPDATE – Staff recommends City
  Council receive and file this update. 1120-04

  Report

ORAL COMMUNICATIONS

ADJOURNMENT

I hereby certify under penalty of perjury under the laws of the State of California that the foregoing agenda was posted
on the City Hall bulletin board not less than 72 hours prior to the meeting. Dated December 10, 2020.

Theresa Devoy, CMC
City Clerk
